title: Protocols for recording morphometric measurement of Indian Pangolin (Manis crassicaudata)
author: Perera, Algewatta, et al.

steps.title: Select and prepare specimen
steps.instruction: Choose a suitable Indian pangolin specimen (live, fresh carcass, frozen carcass, or museum specimen – taxidermy, dry skin, or fluid‑preserved). Ensure the study has ethical clearance from the relevant agency before proceeding.

steps.title: Determine sex and age
steps.instruction: Uncurl the animal (see step 3) and inspect the genital area: males show a visible penis and internal testicles; females have a pore‑like vulva below the anus and may show mammary glands if reproductively mature. Record age class (juvenile, sub‑adult, adult) based on size and any published criteria.

steps.title: Uncurl the pangolin
steps.instruction: Wear hard gloves, grasp the distal end of the tail, and apply a gentle up‑and‑down motion a few times to coax the animal into an uncurled, physiological position.

steps.title: Position specimen for measurements
steps.instruction: Place the uncurled pangolin on a flat surface in a physiological (recumbent) position. For frozen carcasses, thaw at room temperature before positioning.

steps.title: Measure body weight
steps.instruction: Place the animal inside a gunny sack and hook it onto a handheld weighing scale to record total bodyweight (precision ± 0.1 kg). For juveniles and sub‑adults weighing less than 5 kg, use a table spring balance. Only fresh, frozen, or live specimens may be weighed.

steps.title: Take length measurements
steps.instruction: Record the 13 recommended morphometric parameters (see Table 1) using a flexible/cloth tape for most lengths and a Vernier caliper (precision ± 0.1 cm) for snout length, ear length, and hind‑foot diameter. Measurements are taken along the dorsal vertebral line with the animal uncurled or in physiological recumbency.

substeps.instruction: Head length (HL): upper commissure of nostrils to nape.
Head‑body length (physiological, HBL): tip of nose to sacrococcygeal joint following body contour.
Neck circumference (NC): around caudal neck, not too tight.
Shoulder circumference / Axillary girth (SC): measured just behind forelegs.
Body circumference (BC): around middle of stomach area.
Tail length: sacrococcygeal joint to tip of last caudal vertebra or scale tip (tail raised).
Hind‑limb length (HLL): tip of calcaneus to distal end of longest toe pad.
Fore‑limb length (FLL): humeroulnar (elbow) joint to distal end of longest fore‑foot pad.
Total body length (TBL): tip of nose to tip of last caudal vertebra or scale tip.
Ear length (EL): bottom of fold behind anthelix to apex of pinna (both sides).
Snout length (SL): tip of nose to ocular area.
Hind‑foot diameter (HFD): base of metatarsals to distal end of longest toe pad (both feet).

steps.title: Measure claws
steps.instruction: Number fore‑limb claws 1–5 from the inside of the body; measure claws 2, 3, and 4 only. Record linear length with a Vernier caliper and curvature length with a flexible/cloth tape from base to tip along the external perimeter.

steps.title: Count scales by body region
steps.instruction: Define five body regions (head, trunk, forelimbs, hindlimbs, tail). Photograph dorsal, lateral, and ventral surfaces with a DSLR camera (18–55 mm lens). Analyze images in Adobe Photoshop or ImageJ™, marking each counted scale to avoid double‑counting. Include scales that are missing but have a clear scale bed.

steps.title: Measure scale dimensions
steps.instruction: Using a Vernier caliper, measure scale width (distance between the two widest points) and scale length (base to tip). Follow the specific guidelines for the three morph‑types (broad rhombic/scapular, elongated kite, folded) as illustrated in Fig. 8.

steps.title: Count scale grooves
steps.instruction: Count grooves on each scale manually or from photographs using ImageJ™; exclude scales with damaged or worn surfaces.

steps.title: Report data by age and sex
steps.instruction: Compile all morphometric measurements, assigning each specimen to juvenile, sub‑adult, or adult class and to male or female sex for analysis of sexual dimorphism and age‑related variation.
